shots.say: Who lives at the top of the jungle?
shots.tag: hook: who lives at the top

shots.say: A bird? A frog? Or an anteater?
I'm Milo. Let's fly up and find out!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we visit the rainforest, floor by floor.
Look at this tall, tall tree! Who is way up there?
It's Mango! Mango is a spider monkey. She will show us around.
A rainforest has layers, like the floors of a house.
Let's count them from the bottom. One, two, three, four!
Four layers! Four floors, from the ground to the sky.
How many floors does your house have?
Floor number one is the forest floor. Down, down, down!
It is dark down here. Can you see?
Fallen leaves cover the ground. Crunch, crunch!
The leaves up high block the sunlight.
So the forest floor is the darkest layer of all.
Let's squint, to see in the dark. Squint!
Sniff, sniff! Who is that?
It's an anteater! Look at its long, long nose.
Where does the anteater look for food? Up in the trees, or down on the ground?
On the ground! It sniffs through the fallen leaves.
It has a long, long tongue, too. Flick, flick!
Anteaters live on the ground. They do not climb up high.
Anteaters find food with their super nose.
Sniff! They smell ants, and gobble them up.
Can an anteater smell ants with its nose? Yes, or no?
Can you sniff like an anteater? Sniff, sniff!
That is floor number one. The forest floor!
Up we go, to floor number two: the understory.
It is still shady here, under the tall trees.
Plants here grow big leaves, to catch the little bits of sunlight.
Can you make a big leaf with your hands? Open wide!
Look, on that big leaf! Who is that?
A little green tree frog! Ribbit!
The air down here is wet and still.
Does a tree frog like wet air, or dry air?
Wet air! It keeps the frog's skin nice and wet.
Count the drops with me. One, two, three!
Can you hop like a tree frog? Hop, hop!
Up, up, to floor number three: the canopy!
Mango lives up here! Hello again, Mango!
The canopy is a thick roof of leaves, high in the trees.
Above the roof, it is sunny. Under it, shady.
Spider monkeys pick fruit up here. Munch, munch!
And look! A macaw, with a big, strong beak.
What does the macaw grab with its big beak? Fruit, or rocks?
Fruit! The macaw grabs fruit in the canopy.
Flap your wings like a macaw! Flap, flap!
Floor two, the understory. Floor three, the canopy.
Now, the very top! Floor number four: the emergent layer.
Look! A few trees grow taller than all the rest.
Short, short, short, and one tall tree sticks up!
Count the short trees with me. One, two, three!
Is it dark up here, or sunny?
Sunny! It is the sunniest layer of all.
Shade your eyes from the sun, like this!
Who lives up here, at the very top? Look who is coming!
A harpy eagle! It is a very big bird.
Flap, flap, flap! Look at its big, wide wings.
Look down! The forest floor is far, far below.
Many animals up here fly, or glide, from tree to tree.
And butterflies flutter up here, too.
Count the butterflies. One, two, three!
Can you flutter like a butterfly? Flutter, flutter!
Who lives at the very top? The anteater, or the eagle?
The eagle! The anteater stays down on the forest floor.
Let's fly back down. Four, three, two, one!
Eagle, macaw, frog and anteater. Everyone has a home!
Which floor would you like to live on?
Time to remember what we learned!
How many layers does a rainforest have? Two, or four?
Four! Floor, understory, canopy, and the emergent layer.
Which layer is the darkest? The forest floor, or the top?
The forest floor! The leaves up high block the sun.
Who lives way up at the top?
The harpy eagle, in the sunny emergent layer!
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
